text:
Jesse (Product): Quick sync — proposing a small, field-focused pilot for the new recommendations: batching heuristics, prefix caching visibility, and quantization guidance. Need: prioritized scope, launch gates, and acceptance criteria. Customers asking: AcmeHealth and Tutorly. Thoughts?
Aline (PM): Love the pilot idea. Let's keep the scope narrow: 1) batching policy templates (mobile + web), 2) cache telemetry + a toggle, 3) one quantization recipe (8-bit lpq) with rollback.
Ravi (Infra): Heads-up: warmup for cached KV can spike memory on 8x cards. We should limit prefix cache TTL for pilot to avoid OOM. Also need a perf baseline: p50/p95/p99 gen latency before changes.
Carla (SE): From customer calls — AcmeHealth wants explicit SLOs for LLM latency and a safety net if top-level concordance drops. Tutorly cares about prompt cost reduction >20% with <1.5% quality regression.
Jesse (Product): Good constraints. Proposed gates: "no >2% concordance regression on our eval set", "cost reduction >=15% for mobile flows", "p99 degradation <=200ms". If any gate fails, auto-fallback to stable model/params.
Aline (PM): Add acceptance for telemetry: cache hit rate, average batch size, quantized output diff histogram. Make a short eval harness so we can run before/after comparisons.
Ravi (Infra): ops-bot reports current fleet headroom: 
```
ops-bot: fleet-capacity: 72 GPUs idle 14, avg-kv-mem-usage: 64GB, p99-gen: 380ms
```
Ravi (Infra): Suggest pilot uses a canary of 5% traffic on a dedicated pool, scale to 25% if metrics stable after 48h.
Carla (SE): For rollout phasing: Phase 0 = offline A/B with eval sets (concordance + latency), Phase 1 = canary 5% (non-critical tenants), Phase 2 = targeted customer opt-in (AcmeHealth/Tutorly), Phase 3 = GA.
Jesse (Product): Prioritization — must-have: batching templates and cache telemetry. Nice-to-have: quantization recipe, automated quant rollback. Timebox for pilot: 6 weeks.
Aline (PM): I'll draft a compact acceptance checklist. Quick version to iterate in the next 48h.
Carla (SE): One ask: include a debug endpoint that returns cache keys for a request id so we can triage misses with customers. Small effort but big troubleshooting win.
Jesse (Product): Agreed. Next steps: Aline -> acceptance checklist, Ravi -> canary infra plan + memory guard rails, Carla -> debug endpoint spec + customer comm draft. Follow-up sync Thursday 9am. :thumbsup:
